svg.title: The anyio task group inside an MCP client, and the two test failures it causes
svg.desc: The figure has two halves and one subject: the anyio task group that an MCP client owns. The top half is a pair of panels drawn on the same two-lane picture, one lane for the pytest fixture task and one for the test task. The left panel is headed The reflex, a yield fixture, and is stamped every test errors. Its code declares an async fixture that opens a client with async with and yields it. On the picture, the enter marker sits on the fixture lane, an arrow drops down to the test body on the test lane, and a second arrow climbs back up to an exit marker that is also on the fixture lane and coloured red: the group was entered in one task and exited in another, which raises a RuntimeError during teardown. The right panel is headed The fix, open it in the test body, and is stamped no teardown error. Its code opens the client inside the test function itself. The fixture lane is still drawn, dashed and empty, labelled no async context lives here, and the enter marker, the test body and the exit marker now sit in a single row on the test lane, so one task enters the group and the same task exits it. Below the two panels is the verbatim pytest summary, dot E dot E, two passed and two errors in 1.65 seconds, with the warning that the tests passed and the errors are in teardown, which is why a reader opens the wrong file first. The bottom half shows what the same task group does to an exception on the way out. A code block raises a ZeroDivisionError inside the client block, and an arrow leads to three rectangles nested one inside another: an outer ExceptionGroup, an inner ExceptionGroup inside it, and the ZeroDivisionError itself in the middle. Because it is a group inside a group, an except clause naming ZeroDivisionError never runs and pytest.raises on that type does not match, while a recursive flatten helper unwraps it so the test can assert on the members of the flat list. The closing line says both failures are the task group the client owns, and that host code catching a specific exception type around a client call has the second one too.
svg.text: One task group, and the two test failures that fall out of it
The client owns an anyio task group. Enter it and exit it in one task, and unwrap what escapes it twice.
entered in the fixture task, exited in another
The fix: open it in the test body
one task enters the group and the same task exits it
The tests passed. The errors are in teardown, which is why you will read the wrong file first.
The same task group re-wraps whatever escapes it, twice
and pytest.raises() on that type does not match
then assert on the members of the flat list
Both failures are the anyio task group the client owns. Host code that catches a specific exception type around a client call has the second one too.
